I would like to preserve the structure I had before where the new polynomial still returns ('q0, 'q1', 'q2') as "names" even though indeterminate 'q2' does not appear in the polynomial. issue_title: Panic in pubsub.go
issue_body:
Revision: `v4.1.0-beta5`

```
panic: close of closed channel

goroutine 46360 [running]:
github.com/peer-calls/peer-calls/server/pubsub.(*PubSub).Close(...)
	/home/runner/work/peer-calls/peer-calls/server/pubsub/pubsub.go:328
github.com/peer-calls/peer-calls/server/sfu.(*PeerManager).Close.func1(0xc00020e1c0, 0xc0003edd40)
	/home/runner/work/peer-calls/peer-calls/server/sfu/peer_manager.go:588 +0x4c
created by github.com/peer-calls/peer-calls/server/sfu.(*PeerManager).Close
	/home/runner/work/peer-calls/peer-calls/server/sfu/peer_manager.go:586 +0x26d
```

This can happen on a slow connection when the user re-joins without refresing the page, but the old peer connection still hasn't terminated. The solution is either to:

1. Reject the new connection, or
2. Destroy the existing connection with the same ID.

While (2) seems easier to do, it would mean that people would be able to kick other people out of the room just by knowing their ID. Perhaps there could be some unique key that's kept private, and only an "authenticated" peer would be able to overwrite existing peer connection if it exists.

```
< +CGACT: <cid>,<status>

```

Where `+CGACT: <cid>,<status>` can be repeated zero or more times, with a new `cid,status` pair.

issue_title: Flickering scrollbar in Chrome.
issue_body:
In Chrome, the vertical scrollbar in the iframe flickers on and off.

At least it did for me with an interactive video, and others have similar issues elsewhere. See [this forum post](https://h5p.org/node/1117083) on h5p.org.

That post and its first comment also point out the fix: the h5p iframe should have `scrolling="no"`.

I hacked this into my `main.bundje.js` and this fixes the problem.

I don't have the expertise to fix this properly in the source and create a pull request, but I think where I inserted it corresponds to line 42 in `src/js/h5p-standalone.class.js` (I found the correct place by [searching](https://github.com/tunapanda/h5p-standalone/search?q=frameborder) the h5p-standalone code for where `frameBorder="0"` is set).

As discussed in our last meeting, [namespace packages](https://packaging.python.org/guides/packaging-namespace-packages/) could be a handy way to ship useful core modules separately for use as standalone packages. This could be extended to all plugins that could be useful outside of the broader Napari ecosystem, such as [`napari-gui`](https://github.com/Napari/napari-gui).

This would provide consistency in `import` statements regardless of how a plugin is installed, as well as allow `pip`-installable plugins to once again reference themselves in absolute imports instead of requiring all imports to be relative.

## What are namespace packages?
Namespace packages are best explained by a simple use-case. Imagine two packages `foo.a` and `foo.b`. `foo.a` and `foo.b` are independent and can be shipped separately. In this case, `foo` would be considered a namespace package. To achieve this, we have the following structure:

```
pkg-foo-a/
    foo/
        a/
            __init__.py
            ...
pkg-foo-b/
    foo/
        b/
            __init__.py
            ...
```

These are known as implicit namespace packages and they were introduced in [PEP 420](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0420/) (available in Python 3.3+).

In Python <3.3, namespace packages were created using the `pkgutil.extend_path` function under each namespace's `__init__.py`:
```python
# foo/__init__.py
__path__ = __import__('pkgutil').extend_path(__path__, __name__)
```

**`pkgutil`-style namespace packages** shall henceforth be referred to as **pseudo-namespace packages**.

# Proposal
Implementation of this structure would require two main changes:
- all plugins will fall under the top-level `napari` namespace (as @freeman-lab suggested)
- the [plugin import inception setup](https://github.com/Napari/napari-core/blob/b7e07813322e68cc49a5c5e4cf53dee599fbb792/napari/plugins/__init__.py) will be moved to `napari/__init__/py`

## Refactoring existing plugins
Plugins will no longer be importable under `napari.plugins.<name>` but under `napari.<name>` itself. If installed from `pip`, it will also be importable under `napari.<name>`.

For example, the `napari-gui` repository structure will look like so:
```
napari-gui/
    napari.yml
    napari/
        gui/
            __init__.py
            ...
    ...
```

Its specification will change to:
```
# napari.yml
plugin_info:
  plugin_name: gui
  path: napari/gui/__init__.py
  ...
...
```

Plugins using `setuptools.find_packages()` in their `setup.py`s will find that it no longer works. This can be fixed with a simple list comprehension:
```python
# setup.py
from setuptools import setup, find_packages

setup(
    name='napari-<name>',
    ...
    packages=[f'napari.{pkg}' for pkg in find_packages('napari')]
)
```

Plugins that do not need to be served as independent `pip` packages should not place their code under a `napari/<name>` directory.

## Implementation
Only a few functions need to be changed, such as `napari/plugins/machinery/_load:get_plugin_namespace`.

The contents of `napari/plugins/__init__.py` will be moved to `napari/__init__.py` **for use with the `plugins` package only**. It will be a pseudo-namespace package, but will only work if **no other namespace package specifies `napari/__init__.py`**:

```python
# napari/__init__.py
import sys
import pkgutil


class NapariPluginImporter:
    """MetaPathFinder for Napari plugin imports."""
    @classmethod
    def find_spec(cls, fullname, path=None, target=None):
        ...


sys.meta_path.append(NapariPluginImporter)
__path__ = pkgutil.extend_path(__path__, __name__)
del sys, pkgutil
```

Whether `pip`-installed versions or plugin-installed versions have priority is a matter of inserting the importer into the end or the beginning of `sys.meta_path`, respectfully.

According to the [PEP 420 specification](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0420/#specification):
> While looking for a module or package named "foo", for each
> directory in the parent path:
> 
> * If ``<directory>/foo/__init__.py`` is found, a regular package is
>   imported and returned.
> 
> * If not, but ``<directory>/foo.{py,pyc,so,pyd}`` is found, a module
>   is imported and returned.  The exact list of extension varies by
>   platform and whether the -O flag is specified.  The list here is
>   representative.
> 
> * If not, but ``<directory>/foo`` is found and is a directory, it is
>   recorded and the scan continues with the next directory in the
>   parent path.
> 
> * Otherwise the scan continues with the next directory in the parent
>   path.
> 
> If the scan completes without returning a module or package, and at least one directory was recorded, then a namespace package is created. 

This means that if an implicit namespace package is found during the scan before a normal package, the import system will not opt to automatically create the namespace package, but will continue iterating through all candidates until it encounters a valid package, otherwise finally creating the namespace package.

Due to this, implicit namespace packages will never be created if a pseudo-namespace package (which is considered as a normal package by the import system) is present. The code within the package extending its path will be executed, acting it to behave as a namespace package.

Within the import system, parent packages are resolved and executed before child packages. For example, in the statement `import foo.bar`, first `foo` will be resolved and executed, then `bar` will be resolved and executed.

Therefore the plugin core's `napari/__init__.py` will always be executed before subpackages are loaded, allowing it to load all plugin and `pip`-installed packages.

# Limitations
1. no other namespace package may define `napari/__init__.py`
2. due to this implementation, [dynamic path computation](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0420/#id3) will [no longer be available](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0420/#migrating-from-legacy-namespace-packages)

(1) can be resolved if other namespace packages insert similar code in their `napari/__init__.py`

(2) can be resolved by copying the functionality introduced in the `importlib` standard library, which provides a special `_NamespacePath` class that provides this feature

issue_title: Add details on spacer geometry for hydraulic diameter computation
issue_body:
In the RO model, spacers are placed within the feed channel to increase crossflow velocity and provide structural support. 

The geometry of those spacers (e.g., filament diameter) will affect the hydraulic diameter and related parameters such as frictional pressure losses, dimensionless numbers (e.g., Reynolds), and the mass transfer coefficient.  

Currently, we only account for spacer porosity in the 0D RO model (pending PR #61 ).

issue_title: Meridian flip and true/mechanical telescope coordinate
issue_body:
Not sure if this is the right place, but that may concern mount drivers, clients and the INDI framework itself.
 
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Users report meridian flip not occurring with the indi_eqmod driver when the mount is misaligned with a delta RA greater than their HA flip settings. I have a discussion in this [forum thread](https://indilib.org/forum/mounts/8930-meridian-flip-not-happening.html) where I try to explain my understandings.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Clients should use true/mechanical mount coordinate to initiate a meridian flip. If clients use celestial coordinate to initiate the flip with a goto command, the indi_eqmod driver will prevent the mount to be counterweight up in the above situation and the flip won't occur. Adding a true/mechanical telescope coordinate in the INDI standard properties may help clients to easily determine the mechanical position of german equatorial mount. It may default to celestial coordinate for non german equatorial mount or mounts which can not sync. At the moment the only property related to the mechanical mount position is the side of pier which toggles when the mount crosses its meridian (not the celestial meridian). That's what I had in mind when I wrote the driver.  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Add a flip command implemented with a goto which reverses the side of pier even if this results in counterweight up position. Thinking about that, consider the case where the user wants to start tracking with counterweight up (which is possible with indi_eqmod). The target star is east of celestial meridian. Misalignment may be such that the mount meridian is eastern to the target star. Not sure what will happen then.

**Additional context**
I created this issue because I was wondering how sync/alignment is managed in other mount drivers. Considering the lx200 driver which can sync, my feeling is that the firmware simply syncs the encoders. I believe lx200 mounts are fork mounts thus they do not care about flipping (no mechanical risk?). Another case is the syncan driver. issue_title: Diagnostic attribute path not surfaced in error message
Improvements to the simulator class (storing the output, holding the past input, simulating multiple steps and defining noise functions)
issue_body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
1) The simulator class does not currently save the output/measurement in its data structure. This could be useful if do-mpc were to be used as a general modelling/simulation toolbox. 
2) Since the simulator class keeps u0 in memory, making it an optional parameter in the make_step() method would make sense (if the parameter is not passed, the simulator simply holds the past input).
3) It would be a nice feature to simulate multiple steps all at once, i.e: to generate first guesses for the MHE
4) Noise is currently set as an optional parameter in the simulator. I think it would make more sense to have a noise generating function explicitly defined, just as parameter generating functions are defined.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
1) I would modify the simulator class to store the measurement in the data structure. I think this would require some careful reasoning, though, as the y_next that is passed when calling make_step at t{k}, is actually the output at time t{k+1}. A perhaps inelegant way to do this would be to compute the measurement twice (before and after the integration and to store the first). Or we can simply say that the output is stored with 1 sample delay. This choice has huge implications, especially for discrete and/or semi-proper continuous systems.
2) Set u0=None as default parameter in simulator.make_step(...) and treat it in a similar way as the two noise parameters
3) Add N_steps parameter in simulator.make_step(...) and iterate. 
4) Add get_v_template and set_v_fun (idem for w) methods. Actually, thinking very hard about this, i'd move the set_p_fun, set_tvp_fun, bounds, normalization factors, etc (whatever is related to the model) into the model class.

**Additional context**
I have already started dirtifying the code, addressing points 1 and 2. Point 3 requires choosing a suitable output format for the make_step function (a list?). Point 4 requires some more careful consideration as well
here: 
https://github.com/Filippo-Tamagnini/do-mpc/tree/improvements-to-the-simulator-class-%23132

issue_title: Add option `enumFallbackNull = true` to support `coerceInputValues` for serialization of enums
issue_body:
For cases where enum in responses of server can change enum values and we should not fail all parsing we need to implement support of https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/blob/master/docs/json.md#coercing-input-values
for it we add into gradle plugin spec configuration new variable - `enumFallbackNull: Boolean`, and if it true we should generate for all enums default value (if spec already have default value - use it. if no default value - use `null`).

as result we got support of successful serialization of response:
```
{
    "type": "unknown"
}
```
for scheme:
```
components:
  schemas:
    Color:
      type: string
      enum:
        - black
        - white
        - red
        - green
        - blue
```
with generated schema:
```
@Serializable
data class Color(val type: ColorType? = null)
```
and json config:
```
Json { coerceInputValues = true }
```

issue_body:
## Problem
ORT has a nice dockerfile with some default environments precooked.
This is very convenient, but sometimes this clashes with the build runtime of the project

In one of our cases, the projects uses python 3.8 and the version of python in the ORT image was 3.9... so the analyses failed.

## Solution
When the environment is good, the default image is perfect, but we want to be able to bring our own ORT file.

Add input parameter: `ort-file` and when set, don't run ORT, but use the `orf-file` instead.

APM ILoggerProvider Implementation
issue_body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In a netcore application, errors can occur outside of a request (HostedService, Scheduled Job, EventBus). When that happens, APM does not transmit the error because it does not know the error occurred in the first place.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like to implement an ILoggerProvider (much like [Sentry](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-dotnet/blob/d2c16b3f837ce24778f49bc73ec39ab74f9c8470/src/Sentry.Extensions.Logging/SentryLoggerProvider.cs) does it) to send these errors to APM. It would, of course, use the `LogLevel` established in the configuration to decide what to send.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Lots of people recommended using Serilog for logging purposes and enriching it with APM correlation, and I get it. However, I'm not interested in logging for the purpose of logging, using Logstash. I only care about the errors and I think APM should be the one to report it. Right?

**Additional context**
I'm also inclined to improve the declaration of this and other APM features using the IHostBuilder, hooking into the application much earlier in the startup process, but that is a topic for another issue.

issue_title: Extending `zephyr,code-partition` with `zephyr,code-header-size`
issue_body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**

At the moment it is possible to generate images for a specific partition by using `zephyr,code-partition = &partition` in the dts. 

However it is not possible to specify the size of the header. This is specified by e.g. selecting `CONFIG_USE_MCUBOOT = y`.

If it would be possible to specify the header size in the dts by using (e.g. `zephyr,code-header-size = <0x200>` the generation of images for any bootloader would be simplified by creating an appropriate overlay.

The zephyr default that does not specify `zephyr,code-partition` or `zephyr,code-header-size` would generate an image for the complete `flash0`.

A dts that specifies `zephyr,code-partition` but not `zephyr,code-header-size` would generate a image for `code-partition` starting at the start of the partition. Using a dts that specifies an image partition and a storage partition would avoid that the image overflows in the storage partition. This could be the default dts for boards that are using the storage area.

A dts that specifies `zephyr, code-partition` and `zephyr,code-header-size` would generate a image for `code-partition` but starting after the `code-header-size`. This could be specified in a `mcuboot` dts that includes (redefines) partitioning and redefines `zephyr,code-partition` and sets `zephyr,code-header-size = <0x200>`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternative solutions have been proposed in #27974 and #31073 (side benefit).

issue_title: DGC issuing and expiring date
issue_body:
Hi

probably is not the right place to ask this but I hope to get some confirmation about this.

The DGC issuing and expiring date are not included in the DGC JSON schema.
I assume the reason behind this is to use the common payload values "Issuing Date of the DGC" and "Expiring Date of the DGC" (see https://ec.europa.eu/health/sites/health/files/ehealth/docs/digital-green-certificates_v3_en.pdf, page 8, table at paragraph 2.6.3)

I recently reviewed the paragraph 3.3.5 of this document:
https://ec.europa.eu/health/sites/default/files/ehealth/docs/digital-green-certificates_v1_en.pdf
Here the "Expiration time" seems to be related to the signature instead of the DGC expiration date.

The DGC validity period is important for the Verifier app, so I think we must agree about the meaning of those fields.

issue_title: Use aria-describedby to link up inputs to their instructions
issue_body:
### Description
This affects all fields.

Some fields have multiple instructions, in which case the `aria-describedby` value can be a space-separated list of each instruction element's ID (no hash). For example, the lightswitch field has additional visually-hidden instructions to describe the on/off labels.

Some fields have multiple inputs. e.g. date-time, color. In this case I would suggest attaching the instructions to each user-interactable input.

issue_title: Udev rules and TransportError
issue_body:
**Describe the bug**

On my Debian machine with a backport-kernel (5.9.15) the udev-rule

```
SUBSYSTEMS=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="0fd9", GROUP="users"
```
suggested here: https://github.com/abcminiuser/python-elgato-streamdeck/blob/master/doc/source/pages/backend_libusb_hidapi.rst

produces to a TransportError

    raise TransportError("Could not open HID device.")

It turns out that on none of my debian machines my user was part of the **users** group. However, all of these machines were upgraded from earlier versions (this also applies to a raspbian rpi4 - here only the **pi** user is part of users, not additional users added with *adduser*).

I was able to fix the issue by modifying the udev rule based on randomly found similar issues for other projects (e.g.. https://wiki.archlinux.org/index.php/Talk:Udev or https://github.com/stapelberg/openhantek/commit/b02d417c11b3dfbc825bec93192c646d1cdd0f41 )

```
# does not work on my Debian 10 machine
# SUBSYSTEMS=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="0fd9", GROUP="users"
# works
SUBSYSTEMS=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="0fd9", GROUP="users", TAG+="uaccess", TAG+="udev-acl"
# works
# SUBSYSTEMS=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="0fd9", GROUP="users", TAG+="udev-acl"
# # works
# SUBSYSTEMS=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="0fd9", GROUP="users", TAG+="uaccess"
# does not work on my machine
# SUBSYSTEMS=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="0fd9", GROUP="users", MODE="0660"
```

Unfortunately my knowledge of udev-internals is very limited and therefore I cannot propose a "correct" fix (if this is actually an issue). However, my understanding of the **uaccess** tag is that it grants access rights to every logged-in user, which seems reasonable for the use of the streamdeck.

**To Reproduce**

Use and apply the udev rules a proposed in the manual.

**StreamDeck Information**
List the model of StreamDeck(s) you are using here.

**System Information**

Debian 10.7 (buster)

issue_body:
# This bug report was migrated from our old Bugzilla tracker.

**Reported in version:** HG 2.1
**Reported for operating system, platform:** Android (All), All

# Comments on the original bug report:

On 2013-11-07 14:28:54 +0000,  wrote:

> Concerning the recent inclusion of joystick support for Android, it is the case that the testjoystick app does not report joystick motion changes for me (although button events arrive as expected).
> 
> Even the addition of the function call SDL_JoystickEventState(SDL_ENABLE), right after SDL_Init, doesn't seem to help.
> 
> Looking at the Java file, though, it seems like there is more to improve. In particular, the function onGenericMotion from SDLGenericMotionHandler_API12 currently handles only two possible axes of a controller: MotionEvent.AXIS_X (as axis no. 0) and MotionEvent.AXIS_Y (as 1).
> 
> The correct behavior would be to update info for the correct axis.
> 
> For a patch idea, one can take a look at one of my old patches (currently marked as obsolete) from Bug report 1700. For instance, the most recent patch (from March 23rd).
> 
> Note that there are a few limitations with that patch when it comes to handling analog axes:
> - No normalization is done with respect to the info returned by getMotionRange (or getMotionRanges). For instance, I have this old unusual kind of USB controller with 5 analog axes and 1 HAT switch. Although the 5th axis belongs to a usual analog stick, for some reason Android reports it as MotionEvent.AXIS_THROTTLE, with the range of [0.0,1.0]. When the stick is centered, a value close to 0.5 is reported.
> - The HAT switch, recognized by analog axes MotionEvent.AXIS_HAT_X and MotionEvent.AXIS_HAT_Y, is naturally translated to two SDL joystick analog axes, rather than a HAT switch.
> 
> Of course, if the SDL_GameController API is used then chances are that there's no need to fix these, although it can probably improve consistency across platforms by some level (including SDL_GameController mappings).

On 2013-11-11 11:32:24 +0000,  wrote:

> Status update: Looks like some recent changes to the code have made the first two axes functional, and testjoystick reports input from all buttons, as well as the same two axes (or AXIS_X and AXIS_Y in the Android language).
> 
> It is still the case that the rest of the axes, including the HAT switch, seem to be ignored, though.

On 2013-11-11 13:16:27 +0000, Gabriel Jacobo wrote:

> Fixed: https://hg.libsdl.org/SDL/rev/965b7e09c5a8

On 2013-11-11 14:20:49 +0000,  wrote:

> Excellent! I have tested a recent revision of SDL (possibly not the very last one) that includes this changeset on two Android-powered devices, with two USB controllers (via USB-OTG). For all analog axes, including the HAT switches of the controllers, I see illustrations of the input values as expected. The same applies to the binary buttons, of course. So thanks!
> 
> Two notes to add:
> - The axis of one of the controller identified as MotionEvent.AXIS_THROTTLE (which as written both is the 5th and is actually a part of an analog stick) has its motion range normalized as expected. If there is actually a controller for which it should not be done, guess the game should let the player handle it in its own way; Or alternatively, if applicable, use the SDL_GameController API.
> - With the current state of SDL2 in HG, true controller support should be easier to implement in a cross-platform manner, not just for Windows, OS X and (desktop) Linux, but also for Android. I'm not yet sure about that, but this can be a big step forward!

issue_title: Customizable preview portal parent
issue_body:
Currently the preview portals all use the same parent, which is a div added by the DndProvider.

However, if you are dragging something that is itself in a portal that is in a div that comes after that common parent, then the drag preview might be behind that other element.

It would be nice if instead of `DndProvider` creating its own `div` we could specify the `div` to use (e.g. `document.getElementById('react-root')`

The current workaround is to just make our own version of `Preview` and `DndProvider` that use the portal parent that we want to use.

issue_title: Native image should ignore non zip/jar classpath entries
issue_body:
**Describe the issue**
20.3 maven jars depend on `tar.gz` files. A tool, like [JBang](https://github.com/jbangdev/jbang), is free to add these `tar.gz` files to the java classpath because it states:

> Classpath entries that are neither directories nor archives (.zip or .jar files) nor * are ignored.

`native-image` does not behave that way. Instead it breaks when it encounters something that is not a ZIP, e.g.

```
Error: Invalid or corrupt jarfile /Users/g/.m2/repository/org/graalvm/nativeimage/svm-hosted-native-linux-amd64/20.3.0/svm-hosted-native-linux-amd64-20.3.0.tar.gz
Caused by: java.util.zip.ZipException: zip END header not found
[jbang] [ERROR] Error during native-image
dev.jbang.ExitException: Error during native-image
	at dev.jbang.cli.BaseBuildCommand.buildNative(BaseBuildCommand.java:320)
	at dev.jbang.cli.BaseBuildCommand.build(BaseBuildCommand.java:135)
	at dev.jbang.cli.Run.prepareArtifacts(Run.java:73)
	at dev.jbang.cli.Run.doCall(Run.java:62)
	at dev.jbang.cli.BaseCommand.call(BaseCommand.java:80)
	at dev.jbang.cli.BaseCommand.call(BaseCommand.java:12)
```

`native-image` should behave just like `java`, `javac` and others.

The issue is reproducible in master.

I have a fix ready that I'll send PR for shortly.

**Steps to reproduce the issue**
1. Create a java file with `//DEPS org.graalvm.nativeimage:svm:20.3.0`
2. Invoke `jbang --native hello.java`

**Describe GraalVM and your environment:**
 - GraalVM version 20.3 and master

 - OS: macOS Catalina]

issue_title: Matlab R2021a bug - mask initialization
issue_body:
There seems to be a change in when Matlab R2021a handles mask initialization in Simulink. There are currently displacement, velocity and acceleration goto tags in each body block. If a user creates multiple bodies, the mask initialization takes the number input by the user, and updates the names of all relevant numbered blocks using that number.
So vel1, disp1 become vel2, disp2, etc for body #2.

It seems Matlab is now (in 2021a) checking for duplicate goto tags before running the mask initialization. There maybe be a way around this, but it is difficult to know Simulink's order of operations behind the scenes. The easy solution is to report a bug to Mathworks and wait for it to be patched. R2021a was just released 3/15/21, so this version should not be widely used and hopefully patches are released quickly. I'm making this issue so that WEC-Sim users/dev team are aware that R2021a is not currently usable.

I will submit a Mathworks issue on this and if necessary look into ways around this bug.

Adam

issue_title: Potential goroutine leak in storage/cache/subtree_cache.go (method SubtreeCache.preload())
issue_body:
I think there is a potential goroutine leak in method preload() at lines 108-187 of [storage/cache/subtree_cache.go](https://github.com/google/trillian/blob/master/storage/cache/subtree_cache.go#L108).

For instance, assume:

- len(want) = 1
- s.populateConcurrency = 3 
- len(subtrees) = 3

If err != nil at [line 170](https://github.com/google/trillian/blob/master/storage/cache/subtree_cache.go#L170) in the first iteration of the range, then method preload() will return while three goroutines are stuck:

- Two goroutines are stuck at [line 159](https://github.com/google/trillian/blob/master/storage/cache/subtree_cache.go#L159) waiting to send on channel ch which is full.
- One goroutine is stuck at [line 164](https://github.com/google/trillian/blob/master/storage/cache/subtree_cache.go#L164) waiting on wg (which needs the two goroutines above to finish).

A potential fix is to change [line 141](https://github.com/google/trillian/blob/master/storage/cache/subtree_cache.go#L141)  
`ch := make(chan *storagepb.SubtreeProto, len(want))` to 
`ch := make(chan *storagepb.SubtreeProto, int(math.Max(len(want), len(subtrees)))`

FYI, I have found this bug with my tool [Gomela](https://github.com/nicolasdilley/gomela) which is a static analyser for concurrent Go programs. Let me know if you find this useful!

issue_title: Record crashes with locked database
issue_body:
## Description

The issue with multi-threaded writing to db causes crashes due to a race condition. The root seems to be similar to what has been reported in #595, but it is a more general issue - occurs on one machine as well and does not require specific conditions as described in #595.

### Expected Behavior

Recording copes well with multiple topics being discovered while there is also data being written to database. No crash occurs regardless of how much data is being written and how many topics are being discovered.

### Actual Behavior

An exception is raised when recording. This occurs (seemingly) in a deterministic way when the number of topics is high enough (e.g. 500).

```
[ros2-1] [INFO] [1611056622.945250784] [rosbag2_transport]: Subscribed to topic '/rosbag2_performance_benchmarking_node/benchmarking_small_67'
[ros2-1] [INFO] [1611056622.948577997] [rosbag2_transport]: Subscribed to topic '/rosbag2_performance_benchmarking_node/benchmarking_small_171'
[ros2-1] [INFO] [1611056622.951884593] [rosbag2_transport]: Subscribed to topic '/rosbag2_performance_benchmarking_node/benchmarking_small_71'
[ros2-1] terminate called after throwing an instance of 'rosbag2_storage_plugins::SqliteException'
[ros2-1]   what():  Error when processing SQL statement. SQLite error (5): database is locked
```

## To Reproduce

The easiest way to reproduce is to use the rosbag2_performance_benchmarking package with https://github.com/ros2/rosbag2/pull/594. Follow the README of the package.
- build with `--cmake_args -DBUILD_ROSBAG2_BENCHMARKS=1`
- run with `ros2 launch rosbag2_performance_benchmarking benchmark_launch.py benchmark:=`ros2 pkg prefix rosbag2_performance_benchmarking`/share/rosbag2_performance_benchmarking/config/benchmarks/test.yaml producers:=`ros2 pkg prefix rosbag2_performance_benchmarking`/share/rosbag2_performance_benchmarking/config/producers/mixed_110Mbs.yaml`

You can manipulate the mixed_110Mbs.yaml file to easily adjust the number of publishers.

## System (please complete the following information)
 - Ubuntu 20
 - Master branch, #c48471e (current when raising the issue)

## Additional context

I also have a PR that fixes this issue: #603. I believe setting sqlite3 to FULLMUTEX as proposed in #595 is a bit too much (since the usual vectors of messages would then lock inside for each single write), although the performance hit is not very substantial either way since the I/O dominates.

The issue is with that the current locking mechanism on top level (mutexes in writer.cpp in rosbag2, added with https://github.com/ros2/rosbag2/pull/491) is valid only with assumption that all writes of data and all creation/removal of topics are synchronous. This is not the case since double buffering has been introduced in the writer. This also would not be the case if another, non-sequential writer implementation was added, and would be unnecessary for another, parallel-enabled, storage implementation.

issue_title: API to include the correct binaries at compile time
issue_body:
Hey, nice library and I am currently checking what would be needed to obsolete the current LanguageTool backend in https://github.com/drahnr/cargo-spellcheck .

There are a few things which would need to be addressed, the most important is to 
avoid the need for https://github.com/bminixhofer/nlprule/blob/master/scripts/build.sh .
The `compile` feature could gate a `build.rs` file which would prep the data which in turn could be included via `include_bytes!`.
That way, one can locally source the data at compile time and include the source files within the binary, with optional external overrides.
Another thing that would be nice, is documentation on how to obtain the referenced dumps.

Looking forward :100:

issue_title: elect leader (sometimes) fails if tikv restarted
issue_body:
I have a 3-pd, 3-tikv cluster in kubernetes. Sometimes, on a node-preemption, we end up w/ titan no longer able to elect a leader.

we repetitively scroll at high speed:
```
{"level":"warn","ts":"2021-05-16T20:44:54.368Z","caller":"clientv3/retry_interceptor.go:62","msg":"retrying of unary invoker failed","target":"endpoint://client-7e0d1443-ffdb-4066-bd62-429ca9649a46/db-pd:2379","attempt":0,"error":"rpc error: code = NotFound desc = etcdserver: requested lease not found"} 
...
{"Level":"ERROR","TimeStamp":"2021-05-16 20:44:54.681786518","Caller":"db/task.go:193","Message":"elect campaign err","PID":1,"error":"etcdserver: requested lease not found"}
```

This comes from db/task.go:

```
func (t *Task) Campaign() bool {
        key := append(etcdPrefix, t.key...)
        elec := concurrency.NewElection(t.Session, string(key))

        if err := elec.Campaign(context.Background(), string(t.id)); err != nil {
                zap.L().Error("elect campaign err", zap.Error(err))
                return false
        }

        if logEnv := zap.L().Check(zap.DebugLevel, "Elect leader success"); logEnv != nil {
                logEnv.Write(zap.ByteString("key", key), zap.ByteString("id", t.id), zap.String("lable", t.lable))
        }
```

i think its missing some error handling on recreating this entry.

(there are also 3 titan running).

looking in metrics, 2 of the titans are scrolling this message. They each show:
```
curl -s localhost:7345/metrics |grep -v "^#" |grep leader

```

the one which is not scrolling the message says:
```
curl -s localhost:7345/metrics |grep -v "^#" |grep leader
etcd_server_has_leader 0
etcd_server_is_leader 0
etcd_server_leader_changes_seen_total 0
tidb_tikvclient_region_err_total{type="not_leader"} 8
titan_is_leader{leader="EX"} 1
titan_is_leader{leader="GC"} 1
titan_is_leader{leader="TGC"} 1
titan_is_leader{leader="ZT"} 1
```

they do not seem to ever recover

issue_title: Class UI
Implement cslib_string's consist_of
issue_body:
The inverse of 'contains', 'consist_of' should return TRUE only when the given string consists entirely of characters in the char string.

```
*temp ws "abbbababababac"
*gosub_scene cslib_string consists_of "abc"
${cslib_ret} == true

*temp ws "abbbaba bababac"
*gosub_scene cslib_string consists_of "abc"
${cslib_ret} == false

*temp ws "     "
*gosub_scene cslib_string is_space ws " "
${cslib_ret} == true
``` 

@danspinola also suggested we could add an `is_(white?)space` alias.

issue_title: sparseTextureGatherOffsetsARB supported by GL_ARB_sparse_texture2 should only take constant integer offsets
issue_body:
Presently Test cases spv.float16Fetch.frag and spv.sparseTexture.frag use non constant integral offsets which result in generation of ImageSparseDrefGather with ConstOffsets as "Image opreand" bit mask but non constant integer offsets.

As per GL_ARB_sparse_texture2 it clearly states

**Do a texture gather operation as in textureGatherOffset(), but return  texture access residency information from the function and the filtered  lookup result in the out parameter <texel>**

This means these offsets cannot be non constant. Hence this needs to be fixed in TParseContext::builtInOpCheck
